key_big: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract like whole numbers.
key_sub: Write zeros in empty places (4.5 = 4.50, 10 = 10.00) so every digit has a partner. Bring the point straight down, then estimate to check: 4.5 + 2.37 is about 7, so the answer is 6.87, not 2.82.
body_html:
The idea: line up the decimal points

Add and subtract decimals the same way as whole numbers, but first line up the decimal points. Then ones are under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. You can only add or subtract digits in the same place.

Different numbers of decimal places

Write zeros so both numbers have the same number of places. A zero at the end does not change the value: 4.5 = 4.50.

When a column makes 10 or more, regroup just as with whole numbers. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, and 10 tenths make 1 one, so the 1 can cross the decimal point.

Subtract with zeros

To take a decimal from a whole number, give the whole number a decimal point and zeros: 10 = 10.00. Then every digit underneath has a digit above it, and you can regroup.

Example

What is 8.2 − 3.45?

Write 8.2 as 8.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, so 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup, so 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Check: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.20.

Answer: 4.75

Estimate first, then check

Round each number to the nearest whole number and do the easy calculation. 4.5 + 2.37 is about 5 + 2 = 7, so 6.87 makes sense and 2.82 does not. Do this even when you use a calculator: one wrong key or a missed decimal point gives an answer far from the estimate. You can also check a subtraction by adding back: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits (4.5 + 2.37 = 2.82)Line up the decimal points. Write 4.5 as 4.50
Dropping the decimal point (4.5 + 2.37 = 687)Bring the point straight down into the answer
Not writing the zeros (10 − 3.46 = 7.46)Write 10 as 10.00, then regroup to subtract
Forgetting to regroup across the point (4.78 + 2.56 = 6.34)10 tenths make 1 one. Add the 1 to the ones
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (8.2 − 3.45 = 5.25)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller

faq.q: How do you add decimals with different numbers of decimal places?
faq.a: Line up the decimal points and write zeros in the empty places, then add from the right like whole numbers: 4.5 + 2.37 = 4.50 + 2.37 = 6.87.
2.82 comes from lining up the last digits, which adds 5 tenths to 7 hundredths. An estimate of 5 + 2 = 7 shows the answer must be about 7, and the correct sum is 6.87.

faq.q: How do you subtract a decimal from a whole number, like 10 − 3.46?
faq.a: Write the whole number with a decimal point and zeros: 10 = 10.00. Then regroup and subtract: 10.00 − 3.46 = 6.54. Check by adding: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.

items.q: You add 3.42 + 5.17 in columns with the decimal points lined up. Which digit of 5.17 goes under the 4?
items.e: The 4 in 3.42 is in the tenths place. Line up the decimal points and tenths sit under tenths: the tenths digit of 5.17 is 1. (7 is the hundredths digit, so it goes under the 2.)

items.q: In 26.38 − 4.51, the digits are lined up by place value. Which digit of 26.38 is above the 4?
items.e: 4 is the ones digit of 4.51. The ones digit of 26.38 is 6, so the 4 goes under the 6. The 2 is in the tens place and has no digit under it.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 3 + 1 = 4. Ones: 6 + 6 = 12, write 12. Answer: 12.4. Check: 12.4 − 6.1 = 6.3.
Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 + 4 = 6. Tenths: 3 + 5 = 8. Ones: 3 + 6 = 9. Answer: 9.86. Check: 9.86 − 6.54 = 3.32.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 3 + 1 = 4. Ones: 3 + 2 = 5. Tens: bring down 4. Answer: 45.4. Check: 45.4 − 42.1 = 3.3.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 1 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 11 − 3 = 8. Tenths: 2 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 9 = 3. Ones: 6 − 4 = 2. Answer: 2.38. Check: 2.38 + 4.93 = 7.31.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Ones: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Answer: 4.1. Check: 4.1 + 6.3 = 10.4.

items.q: What is 2.9 + 2.5?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 9 + 5 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5.4. Check: 5.4 − 2.5 = 2.9.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 + 6 = 9. Tenths: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 6 + 1 = 12, write 12. Answer: 12.09. Check: 12.09 − 6.16 = 5.93.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 9 + 1 = 15, write 15. Answer: 15.44. Check: 15.44 − 9.48 = 5.96.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 6 − 3 = 3. Tenths: 3 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 7 = 6. Ones: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.63. Check: 0.63 + 1.73 = 2.36.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 18 − 9 = 9. Tenths: 8 − 0 = 8. Ones: 6 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 16 − 9 = 7. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 57.89. Check: 57.89 + 9.09 = 66.98.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 + 5 = 8. Tenths: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11, write 11. Answer: 114.18. Check: 114.18 − 34.65 = 79.53.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 4 = 8. Tenths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 6 = 4. Ones: 8 − 0 = 8. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. Answer: 38.48. Check: 38.48 + 30.64 = 69.12.
Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 9 − 1 = 8. Ones: 2 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 3 = 9. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 19.8. Check: 19.8 + 13.1 = 32.9.

items.q: Add.

Line up the decimal points. Thousandths: 3 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 hundredth becomes 10 thousandths: 13 − 9 = 4. Hundredths: 5 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 15 − 9 = 6. Tenths: 3 − 0 = 3. Ones: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 2.364. Check: 2.364 + 3.099 = 5.463.

items.q: Add.

Line up the decimal points. Thousandths: 1 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 hundredth becomes 10 thousandths: 11 − 9 = 2. Hundredths: 3 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 13 − 4 = 9. Tenths: 8 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 18 − 9 = 9. Ones: 7 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 17 − 8 = 9. Answer: 9.992. Check: 9.992 + 8.949 = 18.941.

items.q: To add 4.5 + 2.37, you write 4.5 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 4.5?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 4.5 = 4 ones and 5 tenths = 4.50. 4.05 is wrong: it moves the 5 to the hundredths place.

items.q: William lined up the last digits and got 2.82. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 4.50 + 2.37. Hundredths: 0 + 7 = 7. Tenths: 5 + 3 = 8. Ones: 4 + 2 = 6. Answer: 6.87. Estimate: 5 + 2 = 7, so 2.82 is far too small.

items.q: To find 12 + 3.48, you can write 12 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 12?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 12 = 12.00. Then the 2 ones sit over the 3 ones: 12.00 + 3.48 = 15.48.

items.q: Ethan lined up the last digits and got 2.53. What is the correct sum?
items.e: 15 is a whole number, so its point is after the 5: 15 = 15.00 (not 1.5). Line up the points: 15.00 + 2.38. Hundredths: 0 + 8 = 8. Tenths: 0 + 3 = 3. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 17.38.
Line up the decimal points. Write 0.6 as 0.600. Thousandths: 0 + 5 = 5. Hundredths: 0 + 7 = 7. Tenths: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 0.875. Check: 0.875 − 0.275 = 0.6.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4.6 as 4.600. Thousandths: 5 + 0 = 5. Hundredths: 2 + 0 = 2. Tenths: 1 + 6 = 7. Ones: 3 + 4 = 7. Answer: 7.725. Check: 7.725 − 4.6 = 3.125.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1.5 as 1.50. Hundredths: 4 + 0 = 4. Tenths: 1 + 5 = 6. Ones: 3 + 1 = 4. Answer: 4.64. Check: 4.64 − 1.5 = 3.14.

items.q: What is 0.6 + 1.69?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 0.6 as 0.60. Hundredths: 0 + 9 = 9. Tenths: 6 + 6 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 2.29. Check: 2.29 − 1.69 = 0.6.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 50.3 as 50.30. Hundredths: 7 + 0 = 7. Tenths: 9 + 3 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 1 + 0 + 1 = 2. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 52.27. Check: 52.27 − 50.3 = 1.97.

items.q: What is 8.58 − 1.7?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1.7 as 1.70. Hundredths: 8 − 0 = 8. Tenths: 5 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 7 = 8. Ones: 7 − 1 = 6. Answer: 6.88. Check: 6.88 + 1.7 = 8.58.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6 as 6.00. Hundredths: 9 + 0 = 9. Tenths: 7 + 0 = 7. Ones: 7 + 6 = 13, write 13. Answer: 13.79. Check: 13.79 − 6 = 7.79.

Line up the decimal points. Write 2.3 as 2.30. Hundredths: 9 − 0 = 9. Tenths: 2 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 3 = 9. Ones: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 10 − 2 = 8. Answer: 8.99. Check: 8.99 + 2.3 = 11.29.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.1 as 6.10. Hundredths: 6 + 0 = 6. Tenths: 5 + 1 = 6. Ones: 3 + 6 = 9. Tens: bring down 9. Answer: 99.66. Check: 99.66 − 6.1 = 93.56.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.8 as 6.800. Thousandths: 1 + 0 = 1. Hundredths: 2 + 0 = 2. Tenths: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 0 + 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 7.221. Check: 7.221 − 6.8 = 0.421.

Line up the decimal points. Write 6.71 as 6.710. Thousandths: 8 − 0 = 8. Hundredths: 9 − 1 = 8. Tenths: 7 − 7 = 0. Ones: 2 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: bring down 8. Answer: 86.088. Check: 86.088 + 6.71 = 92.798.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 40.7 as 40.700. Thousandths: 7 + 0 = 7. Hundredths: 2 + 0 = 2. Tenths: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5. Tens: 5 + 4 = 9. Answer: 95.627. Check: 95.627 − 40.7 = 54.927.

items.q: What is 61.33 − 3?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 3 as 3.00. Hundredths: 3 − 0 = 3. Tenths: 3 − 0 = 3. Ones: 1 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 11 − 3 = 8. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 58.33. Check: 58.33 + 3 = 61.33.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.77 as 6.770. Thousandths: 7 + 0 = 7. Hundredths: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 0 + 7 + 1 = 8. Ones: 9 + 6 = 15, write 15. Answer: 15.837. Check: 15.837 − 6.77 = 9.067.

Line up the decimal points. Write 10.4 as 10.400. Thousandths: 8 − 0 = 8. Hundredths: 4 − 0 = 4. Tenths: 2 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 4 = 8. Ones: 5 − 0 = 5. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 5.848. Check: 5.848 + 10.4 = 16.248.

items.q: To find 10 − 3.46, how should you write 10 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 10 is 1 ten and 0 ones, and its decimal point is after the 0. Write 10.00: two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 10.00 − 3.46 = 6.54.

items.q: Mei found 10 − 3.46 = 6.54. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.00 = 10. You get back the starting number, so her answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00. Hundredths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 6 = 4. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 6.54. Check: 6.54 + 3.46 = 10.

items.q: What is 5 − 2.37?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.63. Check: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8.2 as 8.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4.75. Check: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.2.

items.q: What is 1 − 0.36?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1 as 1.00. Hundredths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 6 = 4. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 0.64. Check: 0.64 + 0.36 = 1.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 7 = 2. Ones: 9 − 6 = 3. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 13.25. Check: 13.25 + 6.75 = 20.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 6, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 15. 15 − 8 = 7. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 4.67. Check: 4.67 + 2.38 = 7.05.

Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.725. Check: 1.725 + 1.475 = 3.2.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 15 − 6.28
items.e: 15 − 6.28 is about 15 − 6 = 9. Only 8.72 is close to 9. Check by working it out: Write 15 as 15.00. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7. Ones: 4 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Answer: 8.72. Check: 8.72 + 6.28 = 15.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 9.45 + 12.7
items.e: 9.45 + 12.7 is about 9 + 13 = 22. Only 22.15 is close to 22. Check by working it out: Write 12.7 as 12.70. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 9 + 2 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 22.15. Check: 22.15 − 12.7 = 9.45.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 50 − 18.35
items.e: 50 − 18.35 is about 50 − 18 = 32. Only 31.65 is close to 32. Check by working it out: Write 50 as 50.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 9 − 8 = 1. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 31.65. Check: 31.65 + 18.35 = 50.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 6.075 + 2.9
items.e: 6.075 + 2.9 is about 6 + 3 = 9. Only 8.975 is close to 9. Check by working it out: Write 2.9 as 2.900. Thousandths: 5 + 0 = 5. Hundredths: 7 + 0 = 7. Tenths: 0 + 9 = 9. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 8.975. Check: 8.975 − 2.9 = 6.075.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 13.4 − 5.825
items.e: 13.4 − 5.825 is about 13 − 6 = 7. Only 7.575 is close to 7. Check by working it out: Write 13.4 as 13.400. Thousandths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 tenth: the tenths become 3, each 0 becomes 9, and the thousandths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Hundredths: 9 − 2 = 7. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Ones: 2 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 5 = 7. Answer: 7.575. Check: 7.575 + 5.825 = 13.4.

items.q: Estimate first, then choose the correct answer without working it out exactly: 0.85 + 2.6
items.e: 0.85 + 2.6 is about 1 + 3 = 4. Only 3.45 is close to 4. Check by working it out: Write 2.6 as 2.60. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 6 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 0 + 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 3.45. Check: 3.45 − 2.6 = 0.85.

items.q: At the school canteen, Harper buys a sausage roll for $3.80 and a juice for $2.45. How much does she spend?
items.e: Put the two prices together: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.8 as 3.80. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.25. Check: 6.25 − 2.45 = 3.8.

items.q: Noah pays for a $13.65 lunch with a $20 note. How much change does he get?
items.e: Change is what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 6 = 3. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 6.35. Check: 6.35 + 13.65 = 20.

items.q: A rain gauge at a Darwin school measured 38.6 mm of rain on Monday and 24.8 mm on Tuesday. How much rain fell over the two days?
items.e: Put the two days together: add. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 4 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 63.4. Check: 63.4 − 24.8 = 38.6.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Amelia ran the 100 m in 14.62 seconds and Cooper ran it in 13.87 seconds. How many seconds faster was Cooper?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 2 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 12 − 7 = 5. Tenths: 5 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 8 = 7. Ones: 3 − 3 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.75. Check: 0.75 + 13.87 = 14.62.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Liam swam 50 m freestyle in 41.36 seconds. Last year his time was 44.08 seconds. By how many seconds did he improve?
items.e: The improvement is the difference between the two times: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 − 6 = 2. Tenths: 0 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 3 = 7. Ones: 3 − 1 = 2. Tens: 4 − 4 = 0. Answer: 2.72. Check: 2.72 + 41.36 = 44.08.

items.q: In the long jump, Mia jumped 3.4 m. Her second jump was 0.25 m longer. How long was the second jump?
items.e: Longer means more: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.4 as 3.40. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 2 = 6. Ones: 3 + 0 = 3. Answer: 3.65. Check: 3.65 − 0.25 = 3.4.

items.q: A bottle holds 1.5 L of water. Ava drinks 0.35 L at recess. How much water is left?
items.e: Take away what she drank: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.5 as 1.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1.15. Check: 1.15 + 0.35 = 1.5.

items.q: A ribbon is 2 m long. The class cuts off 0.85 m for a banner. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take the part cut off away: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 2 as 2.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 8 = 1. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1.15. Check: 1.15 + 0.85 = 2.

items.q: Aarav's puppy had a mass of 4.6 kg. In a month it gained 0.85 kg. What is its mass now?
items.e: The puppy got heavier: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 4.6 as 4.60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5.45. Check: 5.45 − 0.85 = 4.6.

items.q: Perth had 152.6 mm of rain in July and 78.4 mm in September. How much more rain fell in July?
items.e: How much more means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 6 − 4 = 2. Ones: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 4 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 hundred becomes 10 tens: 14 − 7 = 7. Answer: 74.2. Check: 74.2 + 78.4 = 152.6.

items.q: Oliver pays by card for a book at $14.99 and a pencil case at $6.49. What is the total?
items.e: Total means add. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 9 + 9 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 6 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 21.48. Check: 21.48 − 6.49 = 14.99.

items.q: In a relay at the swimming carnival, Zara swam the first leg in 32.48 seconds and Charlotte swam the second leg in 29.75 seconds. What was their total time?
items.e: Total time means add the two legs. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 62.23. Check: 62.23 − 29.75 = 32.48.

items.q: On a road trip, a family drove 125.6 km before lunch and 87.45 km after lunch. How far did they drive altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 125.6 as 125.60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 213.05. Check: 213.05 − 87.45 = 125.6.

items.q: A watermelon has a mass of 3.2 kg. Jack cuts off a piece with a mass of 1.475 kg. What is the mass of the rest?
items.e: Take away the piece: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.2 as 3.200. Thousandths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 tenth: the tenths become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the thousandths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Hundredths: 9 − 7 = 2. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 1.725. Check: 1.725 + 1.475 = 3.2.

items.q: Grace has $25 at the school fete. She buys a plant for $8.45 and a cake for $6.75. How much money does she have left?
A relay is 3.2 km long. The first runner runs 1.45 km and the second runs 0.9 km. How far does the third runner have to run?
items.e: Step 1, first two runners: 1.45 + 0.9 = 2.35 km. Step 2, the rest: 3.20 − 2.35 = 0.85 km. (1.66 lines up the last digits, 1.45 + 0.9 = 1.54, instead of the decimal points. 2.35 km stops after step 1.)

items.q: Matilda records the rain at school for three days: 12.4 mm, 9.8 mm and 4.6 mm. What is the total rainfall?
items.e: Total means add all three days. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 + 8 + 6 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 26.8.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 2.45 = 6
items.e: Use subtraction: 6 − 2.45 = 6.00 − 2.45 = 3.55. Check: 3.55 + 2.45 = 6.00 = 6. (4.45 forgets to write the zeros: 6 − 2 = 4, then brings down .45.)

items.q: William has $50. He wants a pair of sport shoes that cost $37.85. After buying them, how much money will he have left?
A water tank had 85.6 L in it. Ethan used 27.85 L to water the vegetable garden. How much water is left?
items.e: Take away the water used: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 85.6 as 85.60. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 5 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 8 = 7. Ones: 4 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 14 − 7 = 7. Tens: 7 − 2 = 5. Answer: 57.75. Check: 57.75 + 27.85 = 85.6.
